critical_code_review_comments: `LeagueResponse` field mapping in leagues.py grew to ~100 fields with manual per-field .get() calls in _league_to_response. New fields silently drop unless the developer remembers to update both LeagueResponse and the hydrator (exactly the bug that occurred here for default_rookie_aav/minors_cap_treatment). Consider using LeagueResponse.model_validate(league) with alias mapping or a helper that iterates model_fields to eliminate this class of bug.

Two-source-of-truth risk: create_league (line 253) constructs LeagueResponse with a small subset of fields, defaulting all others to None even if the DB doc already has them. Prefer routing through _league_to_response after the initial insert.

rca of the issue: Bug: `PUT /api/leagues/{id}/admin/cap-settings` persisted new fields `default_rookie_aav` + `minors_cap_treatment` to Mongo, but `GET /api/leagues/{id}` never returned them. Root cause: `_league_to_response()` in /app/backend/routes/leagues.py (lines 279-380) manually maps each Mongo field to a `LeagueResponse` constructor arg. When the new fields were added to `LeagueResponse` (lines 183-184), the developer forgot to update the hydrator. Symptom: frontend `SalaryCapCard` would show default 950000 forever, and `useDraftCapView` hook couldn't read the persisted value from league response. Fix: appended `default_rookie_aav=league.get('default_rookie_aav')` and `minors_cap_treatment=league.get('minors_cap_treatment')` to the `_league_to_response` return. Verified via `tests/test_iter232N62_live_http.py::test_cap_settings_put_new_fields` (now passing).
